newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends slightly lower on profittaking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends slightly lower on profittaking.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed slightly lower on profit taking in the wake of recent contract highs in the November contract, traders said.

Forecasts for slowing Canadian exports and tight deliverable supplies motivated early buying in November that carried it to a contract high of $422.20 per tbf. However, late in the session that support waned and prices slipped to close slightly lower.
Although it closed slightly lower, the market remained firm and November's settlement at $418.00 was up from the $395.00 settlement a week ago.
Lumber closed down $0.20 to $2.00 with November off $0.20 at $418.00 and January 1997 off $0.30 at $390.40.
